detailed_description: Excel Merger combines selected worksheets from multiple XLSX or XLS files directly in the browser. After loading files, you can keep only the sheets you need, choose a vertical merge to append rows, or choose a horizontal merge to place columns side by side by row position. The vertical mode builds a shared set of headers and fills missing cells with blanks. The horizontal mode prefixes column names with the sheet name when multiple sources are selected. The tool downloads a new XLSX file and is best for quick spreadsheet consolidation, draft reporting, and preparing simple tables for later cleanup. It does not match rows by a lookup field, remove duplicates, or preserve complex workbook styling.
usage_steps: Upload one or more XLSX or XLS files.
Review the detected worksheets and turn off any sheet you do not want to merge.
Choose vertical mode when you want rows from selected sheets stacked together.
Choose horizontal mode when you want columns placed side by side by row position.
Click the merge button and download the generated XLSX file.
usage_examples: Combine weekly sales sheets into one workbook before cleaning the data in a spreadsheet app.
Collect selected worksheets from several simple Excel files into one XLSX for a reporting draft.
Place two small tables next to each other with horizontal mode for a quick comparison.
Prepare a rough merged workbook before importing the data into an analytics workflow.

faqs.question: Which file types are supported?
faqs.answer: The current page accepts XLSX and XLS files and downloads the merged result as XLSX.

faqs.question: What is the difference between vertical and horizontal merge?
faqs.answer: Vertical mode appends rows and aligns available headers. Horizontal mode places columns side by side by row position.

faqs.question: Does Excel Merger match rows by an ID or lookup field?
faqs.answer: No. Horizontal merging follows row order, so use a spreadsheet or data tool when you need lookup-based matching.

faqs.question: Are files uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: Files are read in the browser through a local spreadsheet library. Review your own environment before using real confidential workbooks.
